sentences.text: The Center is comprised of basic necessity but the buildup area of the residential premises is small in comparison to prescribed norms, specially to the part that the Center is having maximum number of beneficiaries (22) with minimum space for them in the residential premises.
Apart from residential portion, the space of overall premise was apt.
The Centre lacks in many basic facilities which were ought to be granted to the beneficiaries as per the Policy.

Without prejudice to the forgoing, we would also conclude the part that the beneficiaries appeared to be happy and cheerful around the Manager and the staff working around them and there is no doubt on any ill treatment or misbehaviour with the beneficiaries.
OVERALL CONCLUSION:
The Policy dated 05.03.2019, governing Gharonda Scheme is a robust policy but it lacks practical aspects.

For example, the policy grants just Rs. 10,000/- per month for renting the premises of 10,000 Sq.ft. but practically it is not possible for any person/organzation to rent a 10,000 Sq.ft. Area (including Playground) in any tier-ll or Tier - III city.

Further, the concerned officers from Social Welfare Department who are required to inspect the Ghauranda Centers more vigilantly because the anomalies pointed out by the commissioners should have been highlighted much before this inspection.

It would also be pertinent to bring it on record that there is a "Country made Liquor shop" is established right opposite to the Male Gharonda Premises and people sit next to the boundary wall of the Centre.
There is a potential risk and threat to the security of the beneficiaries of the male Gharonda Center.

Looking into the seriousness of the concern, the Court commissioners even met and requested the Collector to reallocate the Liquor shop to a new place, but there is no update on this regard till date and the Collector has replied that it is not possible to shift the Liquor shop to a new place, whereas the Gharaunda centre should be shifted to a new place.
Further, the Funds which are allocated to the Gharonda Centers and their expenditure are required to be inspected in a much robust manner in order to avoid the misuse of the funds.

In final conclusion, we found the Male Ghronda Center to be satisfactory, but the female Gharonda Center needs to be shifted immediately in much better (open)
premises, where at least the beneficiary can enjoy their basic right to free movement.

sentences.text: The Centre receives an amount of Rs. 17,08,920/- per year under the head of salary and honorarium to the employees.
However, upon inspection and interaction with employees it was found that the actual sanctioned amount was not being paid and most of the employees were being paid less.
Furthermore, the Centre receives an amount of Rs. 5000/- per month for Occupational Therapist but no Therapist has been appointed.
It was surprising that no appointment letters were issued to anyone, neither any record was maintained to show that how much salary was being given to the employees.
One register showing dispersal of salary to certain staff was found.
No salary slips were issued.

In final conclusion, we found the Male Ghronda Center to be satisfactory, but the female Gharonda Center needs to be shifted immediately in much better (open)
premises, where at least the beneficiary can enjoy their basic right to free movement.
